statement: The function returns a result r and, interpreting r as an integer, r is the largest k such that there exist indices 0 = b_0 < b_1 < ... < b_k = n for which the concatenation, for j = 0,...,k-1, of the nondecreasing sorts of the nonempty blocks arr[b_j],...,arr[b_{j+1}-1] equals the nondecreasing sort of the whole array arr.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 2000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] <= 100000000.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail (no overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic).
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 2000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, interpreting r as an integer, 1 <= r <= n.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 2000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist indices 0 = b_0 < b_1 < ... < b_r = n (with r interpreted as a nonnegative integer) such that the concatenation of the nondecreasing sorts of the blocks arr[b_j],...,arr[b_{j+1}-1] for j = 0,...,r-1 equals the nondecreasing sort of arr.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 2000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every k >= 0 and every sequence 0 = b_0 < b_1 < ... < b_k = n, if the concatenation of the nondecreasing sorts of the blocks arr[b_j],...,arr[b_{j+1}-1] for j = 0,...,k-1 equals the nondecreasing sort of arr, then k <= r (with r interpreted as an integer).
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 2000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let C be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n-1 such that max{arr[j] | 0 <= j <= i} <= min{arr[j] | i < j < n}. Then r = 1 + C (with r interpreted as an integer). For n = 1, C = 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 2000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = n if and only if arr is nondecreasing, i.e. arr[0] <= arr[1] <= ... <= arr[n-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 2000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 2000, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] <= 100000000, and additionally n >= 2 and arr[0] > arr[n-1].

statement: Let r be the result returned on arr and r' the result returned on arr'. Then r = r' (both interpreted as integers).
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 2000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] <= 100000000. Let c be any integer such that 0 <= arr[i] + c <= 100000000 for every i, and let arr' be the length-n slice with arr'[i] = arr[i] + c; arr' also satisfies the problem constraints.

statement: Let r be the result returned on arr and r' the result returned on arr'. Then r' = r + 1 (both interpreted as integers).
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 2000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] <= 100000000. Let x be an integer with max(arr) <= x <= 100000000, and suppose n+1 <= 2000. Let arr' be the length-(n+1) slice with arr'[i] = arr[i] for i < n and arr'[n] = x; arr' also satisfies the problem constraints.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, let D be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < n-1 and arr[i] <= arr[i+1]. Then r <= 1 + D (with r interpreted as an integer).
preconditions: Let n = len(arr). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 2000 and, for every i with 0 <= i < n, 0 <= arr[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every valid partition 0 = b_0 < b_1 < ... < b_r = n into exactly r chunks whose chunkwise nondecreasing sorts concatenate to the nondecreasing sort of arr, every internal boundary b_j with 1 <= j <= r-1 satisfies max{arr[t] | 0 <= t < b_j} <= min{arr[t] | b_j <= t < n}.
